insights.claim: All three detector types expose unauthenticated HTTP APIs, relying entirely on platform-level network isolation for access control.
insights.reasoning: Both app.py files instantiate FastAPI with no authentication dependencies or middleware. The LLM Judge explicitly passes an empty dependencies list. This is typical for KServe-managed workloads where Istio/service mesh provides network-level auth, but any mesh misconfiguration would expose content-analysis APIs without protection.

insights.claim: The LLM Judge detector has a hard runtime dependency on an external vLLM inference server, creating a failure coupling between the detector and the model serving layer.

provenance.location: detectors/llm_judge/detector.py:25-28 — VLLM_BASE_URL required env var, ValueError on absence

insights.reasoning: Unlike the built-in and HuggingFace detectors which are self-contained, the LLM Judge detector will fail to start (ValueError) if VLLM_BASE_URL is not set, and will fail at request time if the vLLM server is unavailable. This creates an availability coupling that platform operators need to account for in deployment topology.

insights.claim: FIPS compliance coverage is partial: the built-in detector Konflux image inherits FIPS from AIPCC, but the HuggingFace detector uses parameterized base images whose FIPS status depends on build-time arguments.
insights.reasoning: The built-in detector has a deterministic AIPCC base image with FIPS-capable system crypto. The HuggingFace detector's FIPS posture depends on whether CUDA_BASE_IMAGE and CPU_BASE_IMAGE resolve to AIPCC images at build time, which is not deterministic from repository contents alone.
